label: 0–6 weeks
title: 0–6 weeks: Start small.
body: No rush. If you need to fly, the American Academy of Pediatrics says it's generally safe from 7 days old for a healthy baby, but 2–3 months is ideal.
points: Short car trips, with regular breaks
A night away nearby is great practice
Check the airline's minimum age before booking
flightNote: British Airways accepts babies from 48 hours old (it recommends a week); easyJet from 14 days. Born early? Ask your GP and the airline first.

label: 6 weeks – 3 months
blurb: Often a good time for a first trip.
title: 6 weeks – 3 months: A good time for a first trip.
body: Healthy babies can usually fly now. Born early or unwell? Check with your GP first.
points: Lots of sleep can mean calmer journeys
Not crawling yet, so easier to settle
A feed or dummy at take-off helps little ears

label: 3 – 6 months
blurb: Curious, but not on the move yet.
title: 3–6 months: Often an easy age to travel.
body: Babies are alert but not crawling, and nap happily in a carrier or stroller.
points: Ask for a bassinet on long flights (BA's fit babies up to 6 months and 8kg)
Restaurants are easier while they're happy to watch
Naps on the go keep your day flexible

label: 6 – 12 months
title: 6–12 months: More fun, a bit more planning.
body: They're interactive and curious, so pack snacks and a few small toys.
points: They can travel on your lap until their 2nd birthday
Eating solids? You can buy some food there
Check the room for crawling hazards

label: 12 – 18 months
title: 12–18 months: Let them walk.
body: New walkers want to move. Build in time to explore at every stop.
points: Pick places with parks or open space
Plan outings for the morning
Bring a carrier for tired legs

label: 18 months – 2 years
title: 18 months – 2 years: Small choices help.
body: Toddlers have strong opinions. Small choices go a long way.
points: Offer simple choices: “park or beach first?”
Keep snacks within reach
Download a few shows before you go

label: 2 years +
title: 2 years +: Let them help plan.
body: Older children enjoy trips more when they know what's coming. These are general tips, and you know your child best.
points: Show them pictures of where you're going
Let them pack a small backpack of their own
From age 2 they need their own seat on a plane
